title: Region-fuse triage orchestrator and staged load-fuse playflows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create an orchestration layer (triage orchestrator) that ingests alerts, traces, and key metrics to decide staged, reversible mitigations across regions. The controller should reduce noisy, duplicate pages by grouping correlated signals, apply SLO-aware burn-rate logic, and run a predefined mitigation playbook (edge routing, throttling, cache enable, autoscaler adjustments) before escalating to region-level load fuse actions. All irreversible actions require a human safety veto and tenancy-aware exclusions.
background: Recent multi-region incidents showed repetitive pages for the same root cause: KV cache storms and model kernel contention. Operators had to manually correlate traces, pause traffic, and coordinate region moves. Existing alert suppression reduces chatter but does not centralize decision-making or automate safe mitigations. This ticket builds a decision plane to lower cognitive load on on-call and speed up correct mitigations while preserving customer SLAs.
goals: Cut duplicate / correlated pagers by 60% for SLO-related incidents
Automate safe mitigation flows for top incident classes: KV cache storms, kernel saturation, queue backlog
Ensure region fuse steps require explicit human approval
Provide a full audit trail of automated actions surfaced in Console and incident timelines
design_decisions: Use adaptive burn-rate windows (1m/5m/1h) rather than static thresholds to detect SLO stress
Fingerprint events by trace root, endpoint hash, and metric co-spike signature for conservative grouping
Staged mitigations ordered: route to fallback variant -> enable prefix/KV caching -> increase background batching -> tune autoscaler windows -> region-load-fuse (requires veto)
Expose human veto via on-call Slack workflow and Console modal that shows estimated impact and rollback steps
Record every decision and action as an immutable audit record with links to traces and relevant PRs
tradeoffs: Automating more actions reduces MTTR but increases blast-radius risk; mitigate with tenancy-aware guards and approval gates
Conservative grouping may leave some duplicate pages; liberal grouping risks conflating unrelated failures — start conservative and tune with telemetry
Adding orchestration increases code surface area and operator training requirements
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic chaos runs show >= 60% reduction in duplicated pages for grouped incidents
Automated playbook executes reversible actions end-to-end in staging with full audit log entries
Veto flow blocks region drain attempts and requires single on-call approver in Slack/Console before irreversible steps proceed
Post-launch: within 30 days, no unreviewed region drains occurred; incidents show faster median mitigation time by >= 30%
